title: Buffalo Wings
description: Classic crispy Buffalo Wings made using the double-fry technique and tossed in a rich buttery hot sauce. Served with blue cheese dressing, celery, and carrot sticks for the authentic restaurant-style experience.

ingredients.title: For the Wings
items: Chicken wings – 2 lbs (1 kg), split into drumettes and flats, tips removed
Baking powder – 1 tsp (NOT baking soda — this helps crispiness)

ingredients.title: For Frying
items: Neutral oil (peanut, canola, or vegetable) – enough to submerge wings

ingredients.title: For the Buffalo Sauce
items: Frank's RedHot Original – ½ cup (120 ml)
Cayenne pepper – ½ tsp (adjust to heat preference)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Dry and Season the Wings
steps: Pat wings completely dry with paper towels — moisture prevents crisping.
Toss in a bowl with salt, baking powder, pepper, and garlic powder.
Lay out on a rack (over a tray) and refrigerate uncovered for at least 1 hour (up to 12 hours).

instruction.title: Step 2 – Fry the Wings (Double-Fry Technique)
steps: Heat oil to 250°F / 120°C for the first fry.
Fry wings for 8 minutes, then remove to a rack or paper towel.
Fry wings again for 2–3 minutes, until golden brown and crisp.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Make the Buffalo Sauce
steps: In a small saucepan, melt butter over low heat.
Add Frank's RedHot, vinegar, Worcestershire, cayenne, paprika, garlic powder, and salt.
Whisk until smooth and emulsified (do not boil).

instruction.title: Step 4 – Toss and Serve
steps: Immediately toss hot wings in the warm sauce until evenly coated.
Serve right away with blue cheese dressing, celery, and carrot sticks.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with blue cheese dressing or ranch.
Accompany with celery and carrot sticks.
Serve immediately while hot and crispy.

chefTips: Pat wings completely dry before seasoning for maximum crispiness.
Double-frying gives the restaurant-level crispy texture without overcooking the meat.
Balance the sauce by adding more butter for a milder flavor or more hot sauce for extra heat.
Use clarified butter for an extra smooth, glossy sauce.
After saucing, flash the wings in a 425°F (220°C) oven for 2 minutes to lock in the glaze.
